input.strategy_title: Graduate Llama Stack to General Availability
input.strategy_markdown:
## Problem Statement

Llama Stack shipped as Tech Preview and adoption is strong, but enterprise
customers will not build production GenAI applications on a TP component.
Graduating to GA requires API stability commitments, a production support
posture, and closing the quality gaps that TP status currently excuses. The
full inventory of those gaps is not yet known — TP feedback is scattered across
support tickets, and no systematic GA-readiness assessment has been done.

## High-Level Requirements

| ID | Priority | Requirement |
|-------|----------|-------------|
| HLR-1 | P0 | A GA-readiness assessment inventories the gaps between current TP quality and GA bar (API stability, upgrade paths, scale limits, error handling), producing the definitive GA scope. |
| HLR-2 | P0 | Published API surface carries a stability guarantee: versioned APIs, deprecation policy, and a tested upgrade path from the last two TP releases. |
| HLR-3 | P0 | Production support posture is in place: documented SLO targets, backport policy, and supported configuration matrix. |
| HLR-4 | P1 | Safety guardrails via TrustyAI are a supported, documented integration (not an experimental flag) for GA distributions. |
| HLR-5 | P1 | The Dashboard enables Llama Stack management by default for entitled clusters (no TP opt-in gate). |
| HLR-6 | P2 | Documentation is uplifted to GA standards, including migration notes from TP. |

## Affected Components

- Llama Stack
- TrustyAI
- Dashboard

## Out of Scope

- New Llama Stack feature development beyond GA-bar quality work
- Deprecating alternative GenAI serving paths

## Open Questions

1. The GA scope itself depends on HLR-1's assessment — until it lands, the
   size of the stability and hardening work is an estimate.

# GA-readiness assessment for Llama Stack

## Description

Resolve the strategy's central unknown: no systematic GA-readiness assessment
of Llama Stack has been done, and TP feedback is scattered across support
tickets. This epic inventories the gaps between current Tech Preview quality
and the GA bar — across API stability, upgrade paths, scale limits, and error
handling — and produces the definitive GA scope. The outcome determines the
size and content of the downstream stability, hardening, and support-posture
work.

## Scope

- Systematic assessment of the Llama Stack distribution (operator, CRD,
  distribution defaults, published API surface) against the GA bar in four
  areas: API stability, upgrade paths, scale limits, and error handling.
- Triage of Tech Preview feedback from support tickets into concrete,
  evidenced gap items.
- Severity and GA-impact scoring for every identified gap.
- A definitive GA scope document that maps each gap to a disposition
  (fix for GA / defer / accept risk) and identifies the downstream
  remediation work it implies.
- Cross-check of the assessment's architecture premises (CRD surface,
  deployment model, provider integrations, maturity state) against the
  platform's architecture context.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A gap inventory exists that covers all four assessed areas (API stability,
  upgrade paths, scale limits, error handling), with every gap carrying a
  severity, supporting evidence, and a GA-impact statement.
- Tech Preview feedback from support tickets is triaged and reflected as gap
  items (or explicitly recorded as not GA-relevant).
- A definitive GA scope document is produced in which every inventory item
  has a disposition and a mapping to downstream remediation work.
- The dispositions are reviewed with product and support stakeholders and
  the review outcome is recorded in the scope document.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-1 (P0): full coverage — this epic is the GA-readiness assessment that
  inventories the gaps and produces the definitive GA scope.

# Llama Stack API stability guarantee and tested upgrade path

## Description

Deliver the published API stability guarantee required for GA: versioned APIs
on the published surface, a documented deprecation policy, and a tested
upgrade path from the last two Tech Preview releases. This epic's detailed
scope is validated against the GA-readiness assessment's gap inventory.

## Description of dependencies

This epic starts once the GA-readiness assessment has produced the definitive
GA scope; the assessment's API-stability and upgrade-path findings may resize
or reshape this work.

## Scope

- Apply versioning to the published API surface of the Llama Stack
  distribution (the OpenAI-compatible REST APIs and CRD-facing behavior as
  applicable).
- Author the deprecation policy for the published surface and bring any
  deprecated surface into conformance with it.
- Implement and test the upgrade path from each of the last two Tech Preview
  releases.
- Remediate the API-stability and upgrade-path gaps identified by the
  GA-readiness assessment that fall within this epic's scope.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Every published API carries versioning consistent with the documented
  versioning approach.
- The deprecation policy is documented, and any deprecated surface follows it.
- The upgrade path from each of the last two Tech Preview releases is tested
  with passing, recorded results.
- Every assessment-identified API stability or upgrade-path gap assigned to
  this scope is remediated or explicitly dispositioned with rationale.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-2 (P0): full coverage — versioned APIs, deprecation policy, and tested
  upgrade path from the last two TP releases.

# Llama Stack production support posture

## Description

Establish the production support posture required for GA: documented SLO
targets, a backport policy, and a supported configuration matrix. The content
of these deliverables is informed by the GA-readiness assessment's
scale-limit and error-handling findings.

## Scope

- Define and document measurable SLO targets for the GA Llama Stack
  distribution.
- Define and document the backport policy (which releases receive fixes and
  for how long).
- Define and document the supported configuration matrix — deployment modes,
  providers, and configurations supported at GA — consistent with the
  validated scale limits.
- Align all support-posture content with the GA-readiness assessment
  findings and the GA scope document.

## Acceptance Criteria

- SLO targets are documented and stated in measurable terms.
- The backport policy is documented, covering release coverage and duration.
- The supported configuration matrix is documented and consistent with the
  assessment's validated scale limits.
- The support-posture documents are reviewed and approved by the support and
  product stakeholders responsible for GA commitments.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-3 (P0): full coverage — documented SLO targets, backport policy, and
  supported configuration matrix.

# Promote TrustyAI guardrails integration to supported in GA distributions

## Description

Make safety guardrails via TrustyAI a supported integration in
Llama Stack GA distributions, replacing the experimental-flag enablement that
exists today. The integration is promoted against the stable, versioned API
surface delivered by the API stability work, so that what is declared
supported is supported on the GA API. Usage documentation for the supported
integration is authored by the GA documentation uplift; this epic records
and hands off the documentation requirements.

## Scope

- Replace the experimental-flag enablement of the TrustyAI guardrails
  integration with supported-integration status in the Llama Stack
  distribution.
- Validate the integration against the published, stable API surface.
- Record the usage-documentation requirements for the supported integration
  (supported enablement, configuration, and migration off the experimental
  flag) as a handoff to the GA documentation uplift; the documentation itself
  is authored there, not in this epic.
- Provide a migration path for clusters currently using the experimental
  flag, without loss of function.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Llama Stack GA distributions include the TrustyAI guardrails integration as
  a supported integration, not gated behind the experimental flag.
- The integration is validated against the published stable API surface.
- The usage-documentation requirements for the supported integration are
  recorded and handed off to the GA documentation uplift, so the integration
  is documented as a supported integration in the GA documentation.
- Clusters using the experimental flag can migrate to the supported
  integration without loss of function.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-4 (P1): Llama Stack side — the integration becomes supported in GA
  distributions. The "documented" half of HLR-4 is delivered by the GA
  documentation uplift, which owns all TrustyAI-integration documentation;
  this epic hands off the documentation requirements.

# TrustyAI-side validation of the Llama Stack guardrails integration

## Description

The TrustyAI team validates and signs off on the TrustyAI guardrails
integration with Llama Stack GA distributions. TrustyAI itself is a Stable
(GA) component and needs no code change for the integration; this epic is the
cross-team validation that makes the integration's supported status
trustworthy, performed by the team that owns the guardrails capability.

## Scope

- Validation of TrustyAI guardrails behavior when integrated with a Llama
  Stack GA distribution, covering the guardrails surfaces exercised through
  the integration.
- Recording, remediation, or explicit disposition of every defect found
  during validation.
- TrustyAI-side support-readiness review and documentation review for the
  supported integration.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A validation report exists covering the TrustyAI guardrails integration
  behavior against a Llama Stack GA distribution.
- Every blocking defect found during validation is resolved or dispositioned
  with rationale.
- The TrustyAI team records sign-off that the integration is support-ready.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-4 (P1): TrustyAI validation side — the supported integration is
  validated by the component's owning team.

# Enable Llama Stack management by default in the Dashboard

## Description

The Dashboard enables Llama Stack management by default for entitled
clusters, removing the Tech Preview opt-in gate. This is the GA visibility
change for Llama Stack: entitled users get Llama Stack management without
opting in.

## Scope

- Change the Dashboard default so that Llama Stack management is enabled by
  default for entitled clusters.
- Remove the Tech Preview opt-in gate requirement for Llama Stack
  management.
- Preserve the ability to disable Llama Stack management via the Dashboard's
  configuration mechanism, so the default flip is reversible (rollback path).
- Ensure existing clusters that opted in during Tech Preview keep functioning
  without configuration changes.

## Risks / Notes

- Landing the default flip ahead of the Llama Stack GA quality work would
  expose a TP-quality component by default; the change should be released in
  coordination with the GA graduation even though no code dependency exists
  (the Dashboard reads and writes Llama Stack CRs through the Kubernetes API
  and builds against no Llama Stack artifact).

## Acceptance Criteria

- Entitled clusters see Llama Stack management enabled by default, with no
  opt-in action required.
- Non-entitled clusters are unaffected.
- Clusters that opted in during Tech Preview continue to function without
  configuration changes.
- Llama Stack management can be disabled via Dashboard configuration,
  providing a rollback path for the default change.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-5 (P1): full coverage — Dashboard enables Llama Stack management by
  default for entitled clusters with no TP opt-in gate.

# Llama Stack GA documentation uplift

## Description

Uplift Llama Stack documentation to GA standards, including migration notes
from Tech Preview. The documentation describes what was actually built for
GA, so it is authored after the implementation work concludes.

## Scope

Content outline:

- GA-standard documentation for every GA-scope capability, including:
  - The API stability guarantee: versioning approach and deprecation policy.
  - The production support posture: SLO targets, backport policy, and
    supported configuration matrix.
  - The TrustyAI guardrails integration as a supported integration — all
    TrustyAI-integration usage documentation is consolidated here, built from
    the documentation requirements handed off by the integration promotion
    work.
  - Dashboard-based Llama Stack management enabled by default for entitled
    clusters.
- Migration notes from Tech Preview releases, covering the tested upgrade
  path and the migration off the experimental guardrails enablement.
- Remediation of any documentation gaps identified by the GA-readiness
  assessment that fall in documentation scope.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Every GA-scope capability is documented to GA standards.
- Migration notes from Tech Preview are published, consistent with the tested
  upgrade path.
- All documentation is technically reviewed against the implemented behavior
  before publication.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-6 (P2): full coverage — documentation uplifted to GA standards
  including migration notes from TP.

# Decomposition Summary — RHAISTRAT-9014 (Graduate Llama Stack to General Availability)

Strategy: RHAISTRAT-9014 — Graduate Llama Stack to General Availability (priority: Critical).

Triage (Step 0): not below-threshold — the strategy spans three components
(Llama Stack, TrustyAI, Dashboard) owned by three distinct teams and carries a
P0–P2 HLR range; nor docs-only — Llama Stack and Dashboard require code
changes. Full decomposition follows.

The strategy's central unknown (its only open question) is that the GA scope
itself is unknown until a systematic GA-readiness assessment lands: TP
feedback is scattered across support tickets and no GA-readiness assessment
has been done. That unknown changes what the downstream stability and
hardening epics do, so it becomes the Investigation epic below (Step 3
decision rule: YES → Investigation).

## Epic List

| ID | Title | Type | Team | Component | Priority |
|----|-------|------|------|-----------|----------|
| E001 | GA-readiness assessment for Llama Stack | Investigation | RHOAI GenAI | Llama Stack | P0 |
| E002 | Llama Stack API stability guarantee and tested upgrade path | Implementation | RHOAI GenAI | Llama Stack | P0 |
| E003 | Llama Stack production support posture | Implementation | RHOAI GenAI | Llama Stack | P0 |
| E004 | Promote TrustyAI guardrails integration to supported in GA distributions | Implementation | RHOAI GenAI | Llama Stack | P1 |
| E005 | TrustyAI-side validation of the Llama Stack guardrails integration | Implementation | TrustyAI | TrustyAI | P1 |
| E006 | Enable Llama Stack management by default in the Dashboard | Implementation | RHOAI Dashboard | Dashboard | P1 |
| E007 | Llama Stack GA documentation uplift | Implementation (docs-authoring) | RHOAI GenAI | Documentation | P0 |

Teams are inferred from `.context/architecture-context/` owning-team fields
(the strategy has no Impacted Teams table — see Health Warnings).

## Dependency DAG

```mermaid
graph TD
    E001["E001 GA-readiness assessment (Inv)"] --> E002["E002 API stability + upgrade path"]
    E001 --> E003["E003 Production support posture"]
    E002 --> E004["E004 Guardrails integration promotion"]
    E004 --> E005["E005 TrustyAI validation"]
    E002 --> E007["E007 GA docs uplift"]
    E003 --> E007
    E004 --> E007
    E005 --> E007
    E006["E006 Dashboard default enablement"] --> E007
```

Critical path: E001 → E002 → E004 → E005 → E007 (length 5).

## DAG Justification

| Edge | Rule | Rationale |
|------|------|-----------|
| E001 → E002 | Rule 3 (Investigation gate) | The assessment inventories API stability and upgrade-path gaps and produces the definitive GA scope; its outcome changes the size and content of the stability work. True gate: `rewrite`. |
| E001 → E003 | Rule 3 (Investigation gate) | The assessment's scale-limit and error-handling findings determine SLO targets and the supported configuration matrix content. True gate: `rewrite`. |
| E002 → E004 | Rule 12/13 (framework → consumer) | E002 delivers the stable, versioned published API surface; the guardrails integration is made *supported* against that surface. Building the supported integration before the API surface is stabilized would force a second validation pass. |
| E004 → E005 | Step 2 exception (cross-team validation) | The TrustyAI team's validation epic validates the promoted integration; the promotion must exist before it can be validated. |
| E002 → E007 | Rule 11 (docs-authoring last) | Docs describe what was built. |
| E003 → E007 | Rule 11 | Same. |
| E004 → E007 | Rule 11 | Docs describe what was built. All TrustyAI-integration usage documentation is authored in E007; E004 hands off the documentation requirements rather than authoring content, so exactly one epic owns that docs surface. |
| E005 → E007 | Rule 11 | Same. |
| E006 → E007 | Rule 11 | Same. |

Non-edges (parallel work):

- **E002 ∥ E003**: same component and team, but different logical changes
  (engineering stability work vs. support-posture authoring); both gated only
  by the assessment. No edge between them (Rule 15).
- **E006 parallel to everything except E007** (Rule 14): the Dashboard lives in
  a different repo, reads/writes Llama Stack CRs via the Kubernetes API (per
  architecture context, the Dashboard owns no data plane and calls no private
  component APIs), and builds against no Llama Stack artifact. Its coupling to
  GA timing is release coordination, noted as a risk on the epic — not a DAG
  dependency.
- **No konflux/repo/license onboarding chain**: all three components already
  exist in the platform with architecture-context files and are Konflux
  onboarded (Rules 20/25 do not apply).

Rule 19 (safety-critical strategy) was evaluated and does not trigger: the
strategy's core is GA graduation of an existing Tech Preview component, not
the construction of new guardrail/sandbox/RBAC capability. The TrustyAI
guardrails integration already ships experimentally, TrustyAI itself is
Stable (GA), and the integration's correctness is covered by the dedicated
TrustyAI-team validation epic (E005).

## HLR Traceability Matrix

| HLR | Priority | Requirement (abbrev.) | Epic(s) | Notes |
|-----|----------|----------------------|---------|-------|
| HLR-1 | P0 | GA-readiness assessment inventories gaps, produces definitive GA scope | E001 | The assessment IS the Investigation epic; its deliverable is the gap inventory + GA scope. |

Both epics carry the P1 priority of HLR-4. The "documented" half of HLR-4 is consolidated in the docs-authoring epic (E007), which owns all TrustyAI-integration usage documentation; E004 records and hands off the documentation requirements instead of authoring them (revision: docs authoring removed from E004 after review). |
| HLR-5 | P1 | Dashboard enables Llama Stack management by default for entitled clusters | E006 | Independent of the assessment — the Dashboard gap areas (flag default, entitlement) are fully specified by the HLR. |
| HLR-6 | P2 | Documentation uplifted to GA standards incl. TP migration notes | E007 | `docs-authoring` priority exception: strategy frontmatter priority is Critical → epic priority P0. This priority does NOT propagate upstream to E002–E006 (Rule 11 edges exempt from priority inheritance). |

All six HLRs are covered; no orphaned requirements.

- **GA scope is an estimate until E001 lands** (the strategy's own open

- **Priority note, not an inversion**: E007 is P0 via the docs-authoring

  per-rule, recorded here because it reads as an inversion at a glance.
- **Assumption on HLR-4 boundary**: the active code change for the TrustyAI
  guardrails integration is assumed to be on the Llama Stack distribution side
  (removing the experimental flag, distribution config, validation); TrustyAI
  itself is Stable and needs no code change for the integration to be
  supported. If assessment or refinement shows TrustyAI-side code changes are
  needed, E005 grows from validation to implementation.

## Component Mapping Notes

- All epic `component` values are verbatim from `.context/rhai-components.txt`.
- E004's work spans Llama Stack (distribution enablement) and TrustyAI (the
  integrated component); assigned the single most-relevant canonical name
  `Llama Stack` since the change lands in the Llama Stack distribution.
- E007 uses canonical component `Documentation` (docs content work) owned by
  the RHOAI GenAI team, which owns the Llama Stack subject matter; its scope

## Tiered Delivery

Not applicable — no external dependency with uncertain timing. TrustyAI is an
in-platform, Stable (GA) component, so HLR-4 involves no upstream gating.
